free_tier.stated: A large-disk VPS line in New York and Los Angeles, monthly: Starter at USD 3.99 for 512 MB RAM, 256 GB of space, 1 TB a month and a 200 Mbps port; Essentials at USD 5.99 for 1 GB, 1 TB, 2 TB and 400 Mbps; Plus at USD 9.99 for 2 GB, 2 TB, 4 TB and 600 Mbps; Advanced at USD 18.99 for 4 GB, 4 TB, 8 TB and 800 Mbps; Premium at USD 35.99 for 8 GB, 8 TB, 16 TB and 1 Gbps. Every tier has one vCPU core, one IPv4 and full root. Annual promo pricing is lower: a 256 GB plan at USD 11.88 a year, 1 TB at USD 17.68 and 2 TB at USD 27.68, on pages headed 'All Prices are Yearly Plans'.

egress.terms: included monthly transfer of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 TB by tier, with no overage price published on the page read
egress.free_allowance: 1 TB a month on the USD 3.99 plan

tooling: Virtualizor on the promo cards; the storage page itself names no hypervisor, and root access is stated
chaining: the annual promo is the cheap route: USD 27.68 a year for 2 TB is USD 13.84 per TB-year, which is below the object-storage rate the same seeds compare against

limits.value: traffic is capped by tier at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 TB a month, and the smallest monthly plan also caps the port at 200 Mbps, so a 256 GB archive is limited by transfer rather than by disk

reliability_note: the New York storage nodes were being migrated from RAID-0 to RAID-5 across three announcements in 2026 and no page states that the migration finished, so a redundancy claim on this line is not supported by the vendor's own notices

evidence.proved: the monthly table prices Starter at USD 3.99 with 512 MB RAM and 256 GB of space, Essentials at USD 5.99 with 1 GB and 1 TB, Plus at USD 9.99 with 2 GB and 2 TB, Advanced at USD 18.99 with 4 GB and 4 TB, and Premium at USD 35.99 with 8 GB and 8 TB, each with one vCPU and a port of 200 Mbps rising to 1 Gbps by tier
'All Prices are Yearly Plans', with Storage Promo Starter at USD 11.88 a year for 256 GB, Essentials at USD 17.68 for 1 TB and Plus at USD 27.68 for 2 TB, quoted

three announcements dated 18 Jan 2026, 2 Feb 2026 and 7 Mar 2026 state that the New York storage nodes are 'moving from RAID-0 to RAID-5', 'will soon be fully upgraded to RAID-5' and 'are being moved to RAID-5'; the 12 Oct 2026 announcement names no RAID status

notes: A separate record from dedirock.json, which covers the KVM promo line at USD 10.88 a year with 10 GB of disk. The two products differ in disk, traffic, price and purchase path. The affiliate seeds that surfaced this line overstate it in three ways: they print 1 Gbps across all plans where the vendor prints 200 to 1,000 Mbps by tier, they describe RAID-5 as delivered rather than in progress, and one prints a 'Storage Wars' batch that no vendor page read carries. Unverified: whether the annual promo plans are still orderable, because the billing store returns 403, and whether the renewal price equals the promo price.
